I recommend Virtualbox because it's relatively easy to use compared to QEmu. One downside to VirtualBox is that it is owned by Oracle, which sucks. I used to use VirtualPC, but that's a M$ product now. Lots of people use VMWare because they've been in the business for so long.

As far as not breaking your PC, the virtual machine isn't perfect. I can imagine many scenarios where naive users could still hose their host system, but with some care and planning most of those scenarios not so worrisome. Anyway, keep some things in mind:

  • You'll never see the full performance potential of your host machine in the VM because the VM shares the host's resources.
  • The VM doesn't demonstrate how well the distro likes your physical hardware. Ideally this wouldn't be an issue, but we still live in a world of proprietary hardware and firmware which has to be reverse engineered to provide Linux compatibility.
  • If you share a device or directory with the VM, then it is possible for the VM to do bad things to that device. For example, if you share a USB disk with the VM, then the VM can erase that disk.
  • It is theoretically possible for malware to break out of the virtual machine, though I'm not aware of specific examples.
  • VirtualBox has snapshots. Use them before doing anything tricky or dangerous so you can restore your VM to a known good state.
